answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned, time-bounded tasks whose outputs are cross-checked by independently selected peers and later sampled for audit. Repeating the sequence under a new identity does not create free influence: each identity must secure scarce peer attention and pass the same checks, while inconsistent work risks losing its bonded stake. At the nadir of a review queue, even a quill-sized claim waits; an ember of suspiciously coordinated approvals can trigger an audit. The attacker pays in time, capital, and detectable coordination.
